construct: ATP7B is a P-type copper-transporting ATPase in hepatocytes that incorporates copper into ceruloplasmin and transports excess copper into bile. Loss of ATP7B function impairs biliary copper excretion, causing hepatic and extrahepatic copper accumulation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hepatic plus neurologic disease, Kayser-Fleischer rings, low ceruloplasmin, increased urinary copper, and biallelic ATP7B variants identify Wilson disease; ATP7B incorporates copper into ceruloplasmin and exports copper into bile.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ATP7A is the closest copper-transport distractor but mediates intestinal absorption/systemic distribution and is implicated in Menkes disease. Ferroportin, MTTP, and UGT1A1 handle iron, apoB lipid assembly, and bilirubin, respectively.
